overall: Clear balanced report with justified Not to Ship recommendation using relevant case studies. Strong on stakeholder identification and ethical framing, but limited quantitative evidence and no visual aids. Meets all task requirements.

feedback.summary: You produced a clear, balanced report with a well-justified Not to Ship recommendation. Your strengths are stakeholder identification and ethical framing using Engineers Australia Code and case studies. To improve, add quantitative evidence, stakeholder-specific decision guidance, deeper systematic stakeholder analysis, and visual elements to reach Excellent across all criteria.
next_steps: Add quantitative evidence in The Most Ethical Path: include estimated defect probability, health impact numbers, recall costs and fines to move from qualitative-only to balanced qual/quant for C4 Excellent.
Expand C2 conclusion to give distinct decision recommendations for each stakeholder you listed in INTRODUCTION (government health department, chip contractor, end-users) not just Rachel/company.

For C5, add at least one ethical decision matrix or stakeholder impact table/figure and standardise your References formatting to meet Excellent requirement for competent visual elements and extensive references.

criteria.C1: Excellent work. You identified several issues in INTRODUCTION - product safety, professional integrity, public harm, reputation - and linked them to engineering design in a competitive tech industry. Your explicit stakeholder list from Rachel to government health department showed both organisational and societal context.
criteria.C2: Strong balanced discussion in DICUSSION: To Ship or Not to Ship. You objectively weighed pros like competitive advantage/revenue against cons like end-user health harm and integrity. For Excellent, you need decision-making recommendations tailored to several different stakeholders, not mainly Rachel/company.
criteria.C3: Your structure - To Ship / Not to Ship / Most Ethical Path / Recommendation - is logical and your arguments in The Most Ethical Path directly support your CONCLUSION that Not to Ship is most ethical. For Excellent, deepen systematic analysis of ethical issues for all stakeholders individually.
criteria.C4: You used relevant qualitative sources: Engineers Australia Code, VW emissions scandal, HSSIB case, Apple. This shows moderate understanding. For Very Good/Excellent, substantiate arguments with both qualitative and quantitative evidence, such as defect rates, cost estimates, or harm statistics.
criteria.C5: You included required sections and your ABSTRACT is well-focused, but you used no figures/tables and your References have inconsistent formatting. For Good, you need limited visual elements used competently; for Excellent, several types of visuals and extensively well-structured references.
